son: seer — they are (3rd pl.) · also son — perfect auxiliary of intransitives and passive auxiliary (todos son exidos 'have all gone out'; nombrados son; son derramadas 'are scattered')
armados: armar — armed (past participle masc. pl.; vídolos venir armados 'he saw them come armed'; = armados)
por: por — through, along, by, for · purpose, 'in order to' (por el reyno quitar 'to quit the kingdom'); por + inf. 'yet to be done' (tres an por troçir 'three remain to pass'); 'for, on behalf of' (por mio Çid) · also por — 'out of, because of' (por miedo 'through fear'); 'for (that reason)' (por tal lo faze 'he does it for that reason'); 'by way of' (por Guadalfajara); por + noun 'for the sake of' ; por coraçón 'willingly' · also 'for (a price)' (por quanto serié conprada 'for how much it would be bought'); 'by means of' (por carta 'by writ'); 'through, thanks to' (por mí ganaredes 'through me you will gain') · also por — 'on, during (a time)' (por aquesta mañana 'this morning'); 'by way of, through' (por medio de la llaña 'through the middle of the plain') · also por — 'in' after fiar (yo fío por Dios 'I trust in God') · also por — 'to fetch, for' after enbiar/ir (enbiaré por ellas, irán por ellas 'I shall send for them', 'they will go for them'); por cuenta 'by count, in a count' · also por — as (por heredad 'as a possession')
las: el/la — the (fem. pl.); them (fem. object pronoun)
de: de — of, from · also de — by (the agent with a passive participle; = por) · also de — 'by (night)' (de noch), partitive 'of, among' (quinze moros … de los que alcançava; pocas de gentes), 'as' (de ganançia 'as booty'), 'from outside' (de fuera), 'on the right' (de diestro) · also 'about, concerning' (de mí non digan mal 'let them not speak ill of me') · also de — 'as if in' (commo de arrancada 'as if in rout'); 'in the manner of' (de guisa 'in such a way'); 'of, among' (de bivos pocos 'of the living few'); nominalized infinitive (del prender 'of the taking') · also de — 'with' of manner (de fuertes coraçones 'with stout hearts'); 'on' (de pie 'on foot'); 'from' of side (della e della part 'from both sides'); de cabo 'anew' (de + cabo, 'again'); de suso de 'above'; seños … de seños colpes 'with one blow each' · also de — 'in respect of' after an adjective (sobejana de mala 'exceedingly bad'); 'with regard to, about' (me plaze de mio Çid 'I am pleased about the Cid'); 'from, at the hand of' (de señor non ha graçia 'he gets no favor from a lord'); 'from' of origin (de moros fo 'it came from Moors'); 'at' of manner (de vagar 'at leisure', de + the noun vagar) · also de’ — Pidal's de’llaño, read as del llaño 'of the plain' (the article's l run into the ll; a reading, not certain) · de + infinitive after an adjective (de ir somos guisados 'we are ready to go') · also de + infinitive after a verb: començar de 'to begin to' (compeçó de fablar 'he began to speak'), piénssanse de 'set about' (piénssanse de armar), aver de 'to have to' (lo que ha de far 'what he has to do') · also de — 'within' of a time limit (De aquestos quinze días, most likely 'within these fifteen days'; sense uncertain); de veluntad 'willingly'; de + superlative partitive (de los mejores guarnimientos 'of the best equipment')
mio: mio — my (unstressed possessive; mio Çid 'my lord Cid')
çid: Çid — the Cid, 'lord' (Arabic sīdī 'my lord'; pronounced Tsid)
a: a — to, at · also aver — he/she has (3rd sg. present, h-less spelling of ha, as in el rey me a ayrado = el rey me ha airado) · personal a before a direct object (salvest a Jonás; a ti adoro); a + inf. 'to, about to' (tornólas a catar); a tan grand sabor 'with so great pleasure'; a ojo 'in plain sight' · also a — 'into' (sacar a çelada 'to lure into ambush'); 'at, in' (a la çaga 'at the rear'); 'against' (dar salto a la çaga); dative 'to' (a mí dedes); haber a + inf. 'have to' (lo han a far); a + noun of direction (adeliñava a la puerta 'made for the gate') · impersonal 'there is' (aver; es dia a de plazo 'there is (only) a day of the term', the most likely reading of a hard line); ha as auxiliary set after the participle (soñado a 'he has dreamt') · also 'on, at (a time)' (a tercer dia 'on the third day') · also a — 'has' before the participle, agreeing with the object (la lança a quebrada 'he has broken the lance'; a menester 'has need of'); a + dative of the person affected (a Minaya matáronle el cavallo 'they killed Minaya's horse') · a — 'as, for' (tóvoslo a grand fonta 'he took it as a great affront')
los: el — the (masc. pl.); them (object pronoun) · also los que 'those who' (demonstrative use before a relative); los — him, them as object of consejar (commo los consejava 'as he advised them') · also los de 'those of' (con los de Castejón 'with the men of Castejón')
sos: so — his, her, their (= modern sus) · also los sos 'his own men' (possessive with article as noun; en todos los sos 'among all his men')
bien: bien — well · bien — good, benefit (noun; algún bien vos pueda far 'some good I may do you') · bien — very, quite, intensifying an adverb (bien çerca del agua 'very near the water')
acordando: acordar — taking counsel (gerund; se acordando con los sos 'taking counsel with his men', the reflexive se before the gerund; = acordándose; cf. tornós a acordar)
recabdo: recabdo — care, precaution, strict order (= recaudo) · also recabdo — business secured, a sure outcome (con todo buen recabdo 'with everything well in hand') · recabdo — account, reckoning (oro e plata que non saben recabdo 'gold and silver past all reckoning') · also con recabdo — within bounds, under control (non es con recabdo el dolor de Valençia 'the grief of Valencia is past all bounds') · also todo el recabdo está 'every precaution is taken' (Pidal: 'hay toda clase de precauciones'; en Medina todo el recabdo está)
salto: salto — leap, jump · also dash, sally (dar salto 'to make a sortie'; non osa ninguno dar salto a la çaga 'none dares to dash at the rearguard')
en: en — in, into, on · en — of it, thence (= ende; por en avemos qué fablar 'of which we have to speak') · also en — 'as' (en paria 'as tribute'); en essora 'at that moment' · also en — 'among' (en todos los sos 'among all his men') · also en + infinitive 'in (doing)' (en levarlo adelant 'in carrying it forward'); en çinco días 'in five days'
bavieca: Bavieca — Babieca, the Cid's horse (proper name; = Babieca)
el: el — the (masc.) · also el — 'he who' before a relative (el qui quisiere, el que es sobre Fenares); el before a fem. noun beginning with a vowel (el espada = la espada; el algara = la algara) · also el de + place name 'he of, the one from' (mio Çid el de Bivar)
so: so/su — his, her, its (unstressed possessive sg.; so çervicio = su servicio); also seer — I am (1st sg. present; = soy; so ayrado, 'I am in [the king's] ira') · lo so — 'what is his, his own' (neuter article + possessive; lo so puede menguar 'what is his may dwindle') · also so — their (so consejo 'their counsel', so vino 'their wine'; = su)
es: seer — it is (present 3rd sg.) · also ser as perfect auxiliary of intransitives (exido es 'has gone out') and passive auxiliary (la tienda es cogida) · also es — that (apocopated esse = ese, demonstrative; en es alcaz 'in that pursuit', por es logar 'through that place')
la: el/la — the (fem.); her/it (object pronoun) · also la que 'the one that' (Çelfa la que dizen de Canal 'Çelfa, the one they call of the Canal')
seña: seña — banner, standard (= seña; modern seña is 'sign', the banner sense is enseña)
sacan: sacar — they put out, post (present 3rd pl.; las arrobdas … sacan 'the patrols they send out'; = sacan)
fuera: fuera — outside, out of doors (adverb; de fuera 'outside, from outside'; = fuera)
valençia: Valençia — Valencia, the Moorish kingdom and city whose king Tamín is addressed (= Valencia)
dieron: dar — they gave (preterite 3rd pl.; dar salto 'to leap')
menos: menos — least, less · menos fallar — to find missing, to miss (de los sos menos non fallaron 'of their own men they missed no more than fifteen') · also a menos de — 'without, short of' (a menos de batalla non pueden den quitar 'short of a battle they cannot get clear of it')
van: ir — they go (present 3rd pl.) · also ir + gerund 'keep going' (passando van 'they go on passing') · also ir + infinitive 'go to' (le van çercar 'they go to besiege him'; se van tornar 'they go back')
cabo: cabo — beside, next to (preposition; cf. modern cabe) · also cabo — end (noun; fasta cabo del año, 'until the end of the year') · also de cabo — 'again, anew' (que los cometamos de cabo 'that we attack them again'; = de nuevo) · also a cabo de — at the end of, after (a cabo de tres sedmanas 'after three weeks')
ferir: ferir — to strike, attack (infinitive; vayámoslos ferir 'let us go and strike them'; = herir)
grado: grado — thanks (grado a … 'thanks be to …') · also grado — will, good will (de grado 'willingly, gladly'; de grado non avrié nada, 'of good will there would be nothing to be had') · en grado tener 'to be thankful for' (en grado vos lo tengo 'I thank you for it')
álvar: Álvar — Álvar (given name of Minaya, Álvar Fáñez; = Álvar)
e: e — and (= modern y) · also aver — I have (1st sg. present, apocopated form of he, perfect auxiliary: Espeso e el oro, 'I have spent the gold') · also aver — 'I will', the future auxiliary in a split future (quitarvos e … darvos e de mano 'I will free you … I will let you go'; = vos quitaré, vos daré) · also the full verb 'I have' (el sabor que dend e 'the delight I have of it')
minaya: Minaya — the title by which the Cid's kinsman Álvar Fáñez is called, usually explained as mi + anaya 'my brother'
del: de + el — of the (contraction) · also del standing for de + la before a feminine noun beginning with a vowel (del albergada = de la albergada) · also del — 'from, for, because of' (cause; del gozo 'from the joy'; del çerviçio 'for the service')
otro: otro — other, another (masc.; el otro 'the other'; = otro) · also otro día 'the next day'; lo otro 'the rest'
plogo: plazer — it pleased (strong preterite 3rd sg.; = plugo, modern plació)
al: a + el — to the; al menos 'even the least' · also a + el standing for a + la before a feminine noun beginning with a vowel (al espada = a la espada) · also al — 'other thing, the rest' (neuter, Latin alius; de lo al non pienssan nada 'of anything else they think nothing'; distinct from a + el) · also a + el before an infinitive 'on, upon' (al exir de Salón 'on leaving the Jalón'; = al salir) · al 'the other thing, the rest' in al feredes adelant 'the rest you will do later' · also por al 'otherwise, for any other reason' (non passará por al 'it will not be otherwise'); a mí mandedes al 'order me something else', give me another charge (the likelier reading of a terse line)
ovieron: aver — they had, they got (strong preterite of aver; = hubieron) · also ovieron a + inf. — 'they had to, were obliged to' (ovieron a enbiar 'they had to send'; = tuvieron que enviar)
lança: lança — lance (= lanza); ardida lança, 'bold lance', stands for the bold man who wields it
metió: meter — he put (preterite 3rd sg.; metió mano 'laid hand to'; = metió)
mano: mano — hand (sg.); en vuestra mano = 'in your keeping' · a mano 'by hand, hand-picked' (escollechos a mano 'chosen by hand') · dar de mano 'to let go, release' (Pidal 'soltar'; darvos e de mano 'I will let you go')
mata: mata — thicket, scrub; here in the place name Mata de Taranz, which Pidal identifies with today's campo Taranz, a stony plain over the head of the valley of Arbujuelo, between the provinces of Soria and Guadalajara (noun; = mata)
moros: moro — Moor (masc. pl.); a moros nin a cristianos, 'to any living soul' (merism)
que: que — that, who, which; for · also por que — because, since (= porque) · por que — by which, whereby (por que más valdrá 'whereby he will be worth more') · also que — 'so that, lest' introducing purpose/result (que por miedo non dexen nada; por tal lo faze … que no lo ventasse nadi); after después/mientra 'after, while' (después que, mientra que) · also que — than, after a comparative (mas le vienen … que nos le van 'more come to him than leave him') · also que — what (indirect interrogative; dezir vos he que faze 'I shall tell you what he does'; = qué)
fueron: seer/ir — they were (preterite 3rd pl., shared by ser and ir; todos fueron alegres 'all were glad'; = fueron)
contados: contar — counted, picked out (past part. masc. pl. with the auxiliary seer; por ir con él omnes son contados 'men are counted off to go with him'; = contados)
ayuso: ayuso — down, downward (adverb, Latin deorsum; no modern equivalent, closest abajo)
destellando: destellar — dripping, trickling (gerund; la sangre destellando 'the blood dripping'; Latin destillare; closest destilando, since modern destellar means 'to flash')
yúcef: Yúcef — Yusuf, the king of Morocco in the poem, the Almoravid emperor (Pidal: 'emperador almorávide'; Arabic Yūsuf; = Yusuf)
le: le — to him, him (dative pronoun) · also le — him, as direct object (leísmo; si ellos le prenden 'if they take him'); dative (non se le dava 'did not surrender to him') · also le — dative of separation, 'from him' (que nos le parte de so braço 'who does not leave his side'); dative 'for him' (ques le non spidiés 'who does not take leave of him')
ovo: aver — he had (strong preterite 3rd sg.; = hubo; here perfect auxiliary, ovo bastidos = 'he had furnished') · ovo de + inf., little more than a plain past (las manos se ovo de untar 'his hands were smeared'); dont a ojo los ovo 'as soon as he had them in sight'
dados: dar — given, paid (past part. masc. pl.; dados foron 'were paid'; = dados)
sol: sol — sun · also 'even, so much as' (sol non 'not even'; sol non será penssado 'it will not even be thought of')
ca: ca — for, because (Latin quia) · ca — perhaps 'but, whereas' (el uno es en paradiso, ca el otro non entró allá; the sense is uncertain)
muchol: mucho + le — very much, to him (mucho + enclitic le, e dropped; muchol tengo por torpe 'I hold him a great fool'; = mucho le)
gujera: Gujera — Cullera, a coastal town and castle at the mouth of the Júcar south of Valencia (Pidal: Gujera is the Castilian-j pronunciation of Valencian Cullera; = Cullera)
un: uno — a, one (apocopated masc. before a noun)
castiello: castiello — castle (= castillo; here the castle quarter of Burgos) · also the castle of Castejón (el castiello dexó en so poder)
bivar: Bivar — Vivar, the Cid's home village just north of Burgos
fasta: fasta — until, as far as (= hasta)
quel: que + le — who ... him (que + enclitic/elided le) · that ... to him (quel creçe conpaña 'that company grows for him')
se: se — himself/herself/itself (reflexive pronoun) · also se — passive 'is, are' (cómmo se gana el pan 'how bread is earned'; = se, passive-reflexive) · also se — ethic/intensive dative 'for himself, with his own eyes' (él se lo vío con los ojos 'he saw it himself')
tornó: tornar — he turned (preterite 3rd sg.) · also tornar — he went back, returned (el otro tornó a Albar Fáñez 'the other went back to Minaya')
ora: hora — hour (= hora); en buen ora, part of the poem's honorific birth-formula, 'born in a good hour' · al ora 'at that very hour, then' (en ti crovo al ora)
nasco: nacer — he was born (strong preterite 3rd sg.; = nació)
mucho: mucho — much, greatly · also mucho — very, intensifying a predicate (mucho es mañana 'it is much too early, too soon') · also mas mucho — 'more' (mucho as a comparative = más: mas mucho fue provechosa 'was more profitable'; Pidal)
era: seer — it was (imperfect of seer = ser) · era + past part. 'had' (ser as pluperfect auxiliary with intransitives; Minaya assí era llegado 'Minaya had arrived')
lo: lo — him, it (object pronoun) · lo que perdedes 'that which you lose' (neuter antecedent of the relative) · also lo — neuter article 'what is' (lo to 'what is yours'); pleonastic 'it' (lo an, lo han a far; por tal lo faze 'for that reason he does it')
an: aver — they have (3rd pl. present of aver = han) · perfect auxiliary (passados los an 'they have passed'; la missa acabada la an 'they have finished'); an por troçir 'there remain to pass'; an ... ha far 'they have to do, are to do' · also future auxiliary after an infinitive, the split future (ve[e]rme an 'they will see me'; = me verán)
preçió: preçiar — he was esteemed (preterite 3rd sg., with se 'became prized, famous'; se preçió Bavieca 'Bavieca became famous'; = fue apreciado; modern se preció would mean 'prided himself')
cabeça: cabeça — head (= cabeza; ç sounded ts)
ganançia: ganançia — gain, profit, interest (= ganancia) · also booty, spoils of war (de ganançia 'as booty'; feremos grand ganançia 'we shall take great spoils')
su: su — his, her, its · also su — their (aquella su almofalla 'that host of theirs')
mas: mas — but · also mas — 'most' (superlative, = más; en todo lo mas alto 'on the very highest part') · also mas — 'more' comparative (que es mas ondrada 'which is more honored'; = más)
mesnadas: mesnada — household troop, band of followers (pl.; = mesnadas)
robado: robar — plundered, stripped (past part.; la an robado 'they have plundered it'; = robado)
canpo: canpo — field, battlefield (en canpo 'in the field, in battle'; = campo)
entre: entre — between, among; entre X e Y 'X and Y together'
fallaron: fallar — they found (preterite 3rd pl.; = hallaron); fallar menos 'to find missing, to miss', Pidal 'echar de menos' (menos non fallaron 'they did not miss')
marcos: marco — mark (a unit of weight for silver, pl.)
avía: aver — there was, it had (imperfect 3rd sg.; que non i avía hart 'for there was no flaw in it'; = había)
dios: Dios — God · also Dios! — interjection of wonder (Dios, cómmo se alabavan! 'God, how they boasted!')
les: les — to them · also les — 'from them', dative of removal or injury (les tollió el pan 'took the bread from them'; viédales exir 'forbids them to go out')
merçed: merçed — mercy, favor; Merçed! 'have mercy, I beg you' (= merced) · also merçed — grace, favour (con la merçed del Criador 'by the grace of the Creator')
vençieron: vençer — they defeated (preterite 3rd pl.; me vençieron de batalla 'defeated me in battle'; = vencieron)
campo: campo — field, open ground, field of battle (= campo; en el campo 'in the open field'; the element in Campeador) · campo de Taranz 'the plain of Taranz'
marruecos: Marruecos — Morocco (rey de Marruecos 'the king of Morocco', i.e. the Almoravid ruler; = Marruecos)
arrancado: arrancado — routed, driven off (past part. of arrancar, 'to pull out, uproot', here 'to rout'; arrancado es el rey 'the king is routed'; = arrancado, derrotado)
álbar: Álbar — Álvar (personal name, Álbar Fáñez; = Álvar)
saber: saber — to know, to find out (infinitive; quiero saber recabdo 'I want to learn the account'; = saber)
todo: todo — all, every (de todo conducho, 'with every kind of provision')
çient: çient — hundred (apocopated before a noun; = cien)
entrado: entrar — entered, gone in (past part.; f[o] entrado = 'had gone in', a ser + participle periphrasis)
fronzida: fronzir — gathered, drawn up in folds (past part. fem., agreeing with cofia; la cofia fronzida, Pidal 'fruncida sobre la cara', the coif drawn up about the face; = fruncida)
trahe: traer — brings (present 3rd sg., h marking the old hiatus; fuerças que trahe 'the forces he brings'; = trae)
cara: cara — face · also de cara 'face to face, facing the enemy' (lidiando de cara 'fighting face to face')
sobre: sobre — upon, over; here 'on the security of' (sobre aquellas arcas) · sobre Navas de Palos 'above, hard by Navas de Palos' (position along the route) · also 'before, against (a town to be besieged)' (sobre Alcoçer iva posar 'went to camp before Alcocer') · also sobre — 'besides, in addition to' (Sobre aquesto todo 'on top of all this')
están: estar — they are, stay (present 3rd pl.; = están) · also progressive auxiliary with a gerund (bendiziéndol están 'they are blessing him')
fincó: fincar — he planted, set firm (preterite; fincar los inojos 'to kneel') · also fincar — he stayed, remained (el Campeador fincó con su mesnada 'the Cid stayed with his troop'; = quedó)
tovo: tener — he held, he did (strong preterite 3rd sg.; tuerto me tovo 'he did me wrong'; = tuvo)
vos: vos — you (object pronoun, polite/plural) · also subject 'you' (vos, que por mí dexades 'you who leave for my sake'); dative 'to you' (dar vos quiero vuestra part) · also reflexive/ethic 'you (yourselves)' (id vos en algara 'go off on a raid'); dative with an impersonal sense (si cueta vos fore 'if need befall you')
me: me — me, to me · also reflexive 'myself' (fata que yo me pague 'until I am satisfied')
he: aver — I have (1st sg. present; perfect auxiliary, = he, and the auxiliary of the split future, e.g. doblar vos he)
gañado: ganar — gained, earned (past part.; = ganado, here spelled with ñ)
teniendo: tener — holding (gerund; teniendo a la çaga 'holding the rearguard'; = teniendo)
quiso: querer — he wished (strong preterite 3rd sg.; non quiso 'he did not want'; = quiso)
santos: santo — saint (masc. pl.); los sos santos 'his saints' · also adjective, holy (los santos padres 'the holy fathers')
venida: venir — come, arrived (past part. fem. sg. with ser; venida es la mañana 'morning has come'; = venida)
tal: tal — such; por tal 'for such a reason, for this purpose' (= tal)
nos: nos — we (subject pronoun; = nosotros) · also nos — us, to us (object pronoun; atorgar nos hedes 'you will grant us') · also reflexive 'ourselves' (nos partimos 'we part'); dative (la missa nos dirá 'will say for us') · also nos' — non + se (aun nos' van del campo 'they are still not leaving the field'; the apostrophe marks the elision) · also nos — non + se, written without apostrophe (nin amigo a amigo nos pueden consolar 'nor can friend console friend'; mas le vienen … que nos le van 'more come to him than leave him', the no redundant after the comparison)
han: aver — they have (present 3rd pl.; = han); after an infinitive, the auxiliary of a split future (seervos han = os serán) · also han a + inf. 'they have to, are bound to' (mandado de so señor todo lo han a far); 'they hold, possess' (que moros las han) · also perfect auxiliary 'have' with a participle agreeing with its object (la ganançia que han fecha 'the booty they have made')
dado: dado — gift, present (noun; Latin datum) · also dar — given, dealt (past part.; tres colpes le avié dado 'he had dealt him three blows'; = dado)
veedes: veer — you see (2nd pl. present, old -edes ending; = veis)
rogad: rogar — ask, beg (imperative 2nd pl.; firme gelo rogad 'ask it of him earnestly'; = rogad)
manos: mano — hand (pl.); dar las manos = the handclasp that makes an agreement binding · a las manos 'for the hands' (pidió agua a las manos 'asked for water to wash his hands'); bolver las manos 'to ply the hands', busy eating
dixo: dezir — he/she said (strong preterite; x = sh-sound; = dijo)
quandol: quando + le — when … him (quando + le, the -e of le dropped; quandol vieron assomar 'when they saw him appear'; = cuando le)
vale: valer — it is worth (present 3rd sg.; que más vale de mill marcos 'which is worth more than a thousand marks'; = vale) · also va + le — 'it goes on (…ing) for him' (ir + gerund with enclitic le: Yal creçe la barba e vale allongando 'and it goes on lengthening for him'; = se le va alargando) · also más vale que 'it is better that' (impersonal; más vale que nos los vezcamos 'better that we conquer them')
algo: algo — something; the poem's discreet word for money, wealth
delant: delant — ahead, in front (apocopated adverb; = delante)
campeador: Campeador — the Battler, the Champion (the Cid's epithet, from campo 'field of battle')
inojos: inojo — knee (= hinojo; fincar los inojos 'to kneel')
fincaron: fincar — they planted, pitched (preterite 3rd pl.; fincaron las tiendas 'they pitched the tents'; = hincaron, plantaron)
somos: seer — we are (1st pl. of seer = ser)
merced: merced — mercy, favor, grace (noun; Merced, Campeador 'mercy, thanks, Campeador', the word of a suppliant or of thanks; = merced)
bivades: bivir — may you live (present subjunctive 2nd pl., optative; bivades muchos días 'may you live many days'; = viváis)
él: él — he (stressed subject pronoun) · also él — 'him, it' after a preposition, of a thing (a él vino; en él fincaredes 'in it', i.e. in Castejón)
palaçio: palaçio — hall, palace; the main room of a house (= palacio)
ivan: ir — they were going (imperfect 3rd pl.; ivan posar 'they were going to lodge'; = iban) · also ir + gerund, 'were coming to, gradually' (ya lo ivan provando 'they were by now coming to experience it')
posar: posar — to lodge, halt for the night (infinitive; = posar)
unos: uno — some (masc. pl.; unos … otros 'some … others')
ya: ya — O! (vocative particle, Arabic yā); also 'now, already' · also ya — 'would', reduced imperfect of aver as conditional ending, 3rd sg., after infinitive + clitic (pagar se ya 'would be satisfied'; = -ía)
doña: doña — lady (title; Latin domina, fem. of don)
tanto: tanto — so much, so great · tanto quanto + subjunctive 'as long as' (tanto quanto yo biva 'as long as I live')
casar: casar — to marry off, to be married (infinitive; por casar son vuestras fijas 'your daughters are to be married'; por + inf. 'still to be done'; = casar)
aquestos: aqueste — these (masc. pl., 'aqueste' = este with prefixed aque-; aquestos dos reyes 'these two kings'; = estos)
cada: cada — each, every (= cada; a cada uno 'to each one')
una: uno/una — one, a (fem.) · also a una — together, as one (adverbial; hivan a una compaña 'they went together'; a una grant ondrança 'together with great honor'; = juntos)
dellas: de + ellas — of them, about them (contraction, fem. pl.)
sepan: saber — may know, should know (present subjunctive 3rd pl.)
más: más — more; e más 'and moreover' · non más 'no more, nothing more'; por que más valdrá 'whereby he will be worth more'
besáronle: besar + le — they kissed him (preterite besaron + enclitic le; besar las manos, the formal courtesy owed to a lord)
fo: seer (and ir, which shares this preterite) — he/it was; went (preterite 3rd sg.; = fue, restored by Pidal as f[o]; of this part's three occurrences, fo entrado and fo acusado are periphrastic/passive ser + past part. constructions, while fo algo is a plain copula with a pronoun predicate, 'was something') · also commo fo tu voluntad, ca fo tu voluntad 'as/for it was your will' (ser + noun subject, 'it was'; Pidal restores f[o]) · also se fo acomendar 'went to commend himself' (ir); fo de noch 'it was night' (ser de + noun, 'night had come'); fo desenparada (passive, 'was abandoned') · also fo — went (ir; mañanas fo Minaya 'in the morning Minaya went'); fo de moros 'it came from the Moors' (ser de + noun of origin; Pidal restores f[o]) · also fo — it was, ser + adjective predicate (Buena fo la de Valençia 'good was the (capture) of Valencia'; Pidal restores f[o])
alegría: alegría — joy, gladness (fizo grant alegría 'he showed great joy'; = alegría)
commo: commo — as, like (spelling variant of como) · how, that, in the way that (commo sirva a doña Ximena 'how he is to serve doña Ximena'); like (commo la uña de la carne) · also commo si + imperfect subjunctive — 'as if' (commo si escapasse 'as if he were fleeing') · commo que 'as one who' (commo que ira a de rey … es echado 'as one who has the king's anger and is cast out') · also commo — 'as soon as, when' (commo gelo a dicho 'as soon as he told it him'); 'since, as' (commo fío por Dios 'as I trust in God')
yentes: yente — people, folk (= gente; y- from Latin g-)
armas: arma — weapon, arms (pl.; armas de lidiar 'weapons for fighting'; en armas 'in arms, armed'; = armas) · also armas — men-at-arms, armed men (treynta mill de armas 'thirty thousand armed men')
ellos: ellos — they, them (stressed 3rd pl. masc. pronoun)
quiérovos: querer + vos — I want (to) you (quiero, present 1st sg., + enclitic vos; Quiérovos dezir 'I want to tell you'; = os quiero)
pudieron: poder — they could, managed to (strong preterite 3rd pl.; los ques pudieron escapar 'those who were able to escape'; = pudieron)
andan: andar — they go about, range (present 3rd pl.; = andan)
ha: aver — he has (3rd sg. present; = ha) · ha — to (a with h-, aver a + inf. 'will, must': lo an todos ha far 'all are to do it'); aver — has, possesses (las fijas que ha 'the daughters she has') · also ha — future ending after infinitive + clitics, the split future (tornar nos la ha 'he will give it back to us'; = nos la tornará) · also ha — there is, there are (impersonal; dos señas ha cabdales 'there are two chief banners'; = hay) · also ha — perfect auxiliary 'has' before the participle (ha vendido 'has sold'; fechos los ha ricos 'has made them rich') · also 'has, gets' (de señor non ha graçia 'he has no favor from a lord') · also ha de + inf. 'is to' (que los ha de aguardar 'who is to attend them'; aver de + infinitive, = ha de)
qui: qui — he who, whoever (old relative pronoun, Latin qui; = quien) · also qui — who? (interrogative; ¿qui los podrié contar? 'who could count them?'; = quién)
ganado: ganar — captured, won (past part.; el castiello ganado a 'he has taken the castle', aver + participle; = ganado)
y: y — and (rarer spelling of e) · also y — there (adverb, = i, Latin ibi; entraré y 'I shall enter there')
maguer: maguer — although (a rare word, of Greek origin)
contado: contar — renowned, esteemed (past part. used as a standing epithet of the Campeador) · also of others: un Burgalés contado, 'a renowned man of Burgos' (Martín Antolínez)
cayeron: caer — they fell (preterite 3rd pl.; cayeron çient marcos 'a hundred marks fell to them', i.e. came to each one's share; = cayeron)
tantos: tanto — so many (masc. pl.; tantos pendones 'so many pennons'; a la tornada … otros tantos 'as many more'; = tantos)
fincar: fincar — to stay, remain (infinitive; = quedarse, closest quedar) · also fincar — to pitch, plant (tiendas a fincar 'to pitch tents'; = hincar)
pagados: pagar — paid, satisfied (past part. masc. pl.; todos sodes pagados 'you are all satisfied'; = pagados)
tanta: tanto — so many, so much (fem. sg. used collectively; tanta adágara 'so many a shield'; = tanta)
dos: dos — two · also do + se, 'when/where … (they)' (Dos fallan con los moros 'when they come upon the Moors', Pidal 'cuando se encuentran'; = cuando se encuentran)
tendales: tendal — tent-pole (pl.; Pidal: 'los postes sobre que están armadas las tiendas'; acostarse los tendales 'the tent-poles lean over and fall'; = postes de la tienda)
mandó: mandar — he ordered (preterite 3rd sg.; = mandó) · also mandar — 'he held, governed' a place (Çorita mandó 'he held Çorita'; el que mandó a Mont Mayor 'he who governed Mont Mayor')
fita: Fita — Hita, town in Guadalajara province (f- for h-; = Hita; traditional identification) · also fito — fixed, pitched (past part. fem., Latin fictus; una tienda fita 'one tent left pitched'; = hincada)
dent: dent — of it, thereof (de + ent, a form of ende 'thence'; non nos darán dent nada 'they will give us none of it'; = de ello) · also dent — from there, thence (dent corre mio Çid a Huesa 'from there the Çid raids to Huesa'; = de allí)
enbiar: enbiar — to send (infinitive; fizo enbiar por la tienda 'he had (someone) send for the tent'; = enviar)
alfonsso: Alfonsso — Alfonso (VI, king of León and Castile)
castellano: castellano — Castilian, of Castile (el Castellano, epithet of Alfonso as king of Castile; = castellano) · also el Castellano — an epithet of the Cid himself (mio Çid Roy Díaz el Castellano 'the Castilian')
nuevas: nueva — news, tidings (fem. pl.; sus nuevas legavan 'his news was arriving'; = noticias, nuevas) · also nuevas — renown, fame (las nuevas de mio Çid sonando van; Pidal 'renombre, fama') · also nuevas — affairs, doings (las nuevas del cavallero 'the knight's affairs'; Pidal 'los asuntos, los negocios') · also nuevas — exploits, deeds (las nuevas que faze el Campeador; Pidal 'las hazañas que hace')
avíe: aver — he had, was having (imperfect 3rd sg., -íe; avíe guerra tan grand 'he was engaged in so great a war'; = tenía, había)
aquestas: aqueste — these (fem. pl. demonstrative, reinforced; = estas)
tantas: tanto — so many (fem. pl.; tantas lanças 'so many lances'; = tantas)
entrados: entrar — entered (past part. masc. pl. with ser; Entrados son 'they have entered'; = entrados)
don: don — don, lord (honorific title) · also don — gift (noun; en don 'as a gift') · also don — from where, whence (= donde, de onde; Castejón don abremos grand enpara 'Castejón, from which we shall have great protection') · 'whereof, with which' (Pidal 'de lo cual'; don yo sea pagado 'whereof I may be satisfied') · also don — when, where (= donde, of time; Don llegan los otros 'when the others come up')
jerome: Jerome — Jerónimo, the Cid's bishop of Valencia (Pidal restores Jero[me], 'don Jerome'; = Jerónimo)
caboso: caboso — accomplished, excellent (adj., also used alone as a noun, 'the excellent one')
coronado: coronado — tonsured one, cleric (past part. used as noun; 'un coronado' is a priest with the tonsure 'crown' shaved on his head; modern coronado = 'crowned', so the sense differs; Pidal: 'clérigo'; = clérigo)
lidiar: lidiar — to fight (infinitive; = lidiar, closest luchar)
amas: amos — both (fem. pl., Latin ambas; las manos amas 'both hands'; = ambas)
rodrigo: Rodrigo — Rodrigo, the Cid's given name (= Rodrigo)
quinta: quinta — fifth, the fifth part of the booty, a share due by custom (= quinta; legal quinto, 'a fifth')
l: le — to him (elided before vowel: l'an = le han) · also 'l = el, the article cut after a vowel (todo 'l día 'all the day')
mandado: mandado — message, news, word (noun; from mandar 'to send, order') · also mandado — order, command (mandado de so señor 'the lord's command'); fazer mandado 'to send word' · also past part. 'granted, assigned' (el quinto que me avedes mandado 'the fifth you have granted me')
